step1_analysis.description: A single-stage common-source amplifier utilizing an NMOS input transistor and a PMOS active load. It is likely a core gain stage of the Low Noise Amplifier (LNA) or IF amplifier mentioned in the paper, providing voltage gain for RF signals around 1.9 GHz.

paper_reference.title: Low-Voltage 1.9-GHz Front-End Receiver in 0.5-m CMOS Technology

DC_Power.description: Total DC power consumption of the amplifier stage.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Calculated using SKY130 square-law parameters for the given bias voltage of 0.9V.

Low_Freq_Gain.description: Maximum voltage gain at low frequencies.

sky130_expected.calculation: gm_n = 2*Id/Vov_n = 559 uS. Rout = ro_n || ro_p = 173k || 173k = 86.5 kOhm. Gain = gm * Rout = 48.3 V/V = 33.6 dB.

Gain_1_9GHz.description: Voltage gain at the target operating frequency of 1.9 GHz.

sky130_expected.calculation: Assuming a 10fF load capacitance, the dominant pole is at ~180 MHz. At 1.9 GHz (approx 1 decade higher), the gain drops by ~20 dB from the low-frequency value (33.6 - 20 = 13.6 dB).
sky130_expected.reasoning: Matches the 15 dB LNA gain reported in the paper, adjusted for a generic 10fF parasitic load in SKY130.

Bandwidth_3dB.description: The frequency at which the voltage gain drops by 3 dB from its maximum low-frequency value.

sky130_expected.calculation: f_3dB = 1 / (2 * pi * Rout * Cload) = 1 / (2 * pi * 86.5k * 10fF) = 184 MHz.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Depends heavily on the assumed output load capacitance (10fF).

Noise_Figure.description: Noise figure of the amplifier at 1.9 GHz.

sky130_expected.calculation: Depends on gm and source resistance. Minimum NF is typically 1-2 dB for modern CMOS LNAs.
sky130_expected.reasoning: SKY130 has a higher fT than 0.5um CMOS, so the noise figure should be comparable or slightly better.

step3_testbench.description: Testbench to measure DC power, low-frequency gain, 1.9 GHz gain, 3-dB bandwidth, and transient output swing of the common-source amplifier.
step3_testbench.spice:
* Common-Source Amplifier Testbench
.lib "${SKY130_PDK}" tt

.param W_xm1=5u L_xm1=0.5u
.param W_xm2=5u L_xm2=0.5u

XM1 N0 LABEL_NET_1 N3 VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xm1} w={W_xm1}
XM2 N3 N1 N2 GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm2} w={W_xm2}

* Power Supplies
VVDD VDD 0 1.8
V_N0 N0 0 1.8
V_N2 N2 0 0
VGND GND 0 0

* PMOS Active Load Bias
VLABEL_NET_1 LABEL_NET_1 0 0.9

* Self-bias feedback resistor to keep NMOS in saturation
Rbias N3 N1 10Meg

* AC and Transient Input Source
Cac IN_AC N1 1u
Vac IN_AC 0 DC 0 AC 1 SIN(0 10m 1.9G)

* Load capacitance to simulate next stage / parasitics
Cload N3 0 10f

.control
  * DC Operating Point
  op
  let power = -(i(VVDD) + i(V_N0)) * 1.8
  let v_out_dc = v(N3)
  print power v_out_dc

  * AC Analysis
  ac dec 100 1k 10G
  let gain_db = vdb(N3)
  meas ac low_freq_gain find gain_db at=10k
  meas ac gain_19g find gain_db at=1.9G
  
  let gain_3db = low_freq_gain - 3
  meas ac bw_3db when gain_db=gain_3db fall=1

  * Transient Analysis
  tran 10p 5n
  meas tran vout_max max v(N3) from=2n to=5n
  meas tran vout_min min v(N3) from=2n to=5n
  let vout_pp = vout_max - vout_min
  print vout_pp

  quit
.endc
